criteria.evidence: Four hill planes grow darker toward the foreground; the dark wing silhouette separates from the pale sky.
The dragon has visible airborne feet and raised wings, an open jaw emitting green fire, and a clearly hilly setting.

review.reviewer: Codex visual inspection of rendered image and requested detail crops
review.strengths: Dragon separates against a light cloud opening; green fire leads toward the layered rolling landscape.
review.weaknesses: Rigid wing edges and broad flat contour bands still dominate the creature. The next stage must develop form before adding more noise.

criteria.evidence: Wing tendons meet at the shoulder, the neck joins the skull, and the hocks, toes and counterbalancing tail are distinguishable.
Lighter upper neck and membrane planes contrast with the underside and cooler far wing; the result remains a stylized painted form rather than realism.

review.reviewer: Codex visual inspection of rendered image and requested detail crops
review.strengths: The shoulder, neck and ribcage now have broken light and shadow planes; the wings separate with warmer near and cooler far paint.
review.weaknesses: The wing pose remains stiff and the head stylized. The canvas weave is too prominent and hill edges are too mechanically smooth; reduce these in materials and finish.

criteria.evidence: Membrane strokes follow the wing fingers, smaller curved marks follow the torso and neck, and horizontal marks build the landscape.
Distant hills are lighter and less detailed than the foreground vegetation; reduced weave no longer dominates the canvas.

review.reviewer: Codex visual inspection of rendered image and requested detail crops
review.strengths: Broken directional marks describe membrane, scales and clouds; the lighter distance and darker foreground remain coherent.
review.weaknesses: Hill silhouettes remain mathematically smooth, and the dragon head and feet still have a cut-paper quality. This is an oil-inspired illustration rather than a convincing traditional oil study.

criteria.evidence: The head and green flame have the sharpest local contrast, while the muted landscape remains subordinate and readable.
Warm near-wing paint, cool far-wing shadows, restrained canvas texture and broken landscape brushwork share a consistent muted palette with the green focal accent.

review.reviewer: Codex visual inspection of rendered image and requested detail crops
review.strengths: The bright green fire and detailed skull lead the eye; curved brushwork and slight edge irregularity better integrate the creature with the painted hills.
review.weaknesses: The near wing remains stiff, teeth and claws are conspicuously geometric, and the scene is closer to a stylized fantasy illustration with oil brushwork than an accomplished traditional oil painting. Further art-direction trials are needed before claiming excellent arbitrary art.

plan.brief: Create a dragon mid flight breathing green fire across a hilly landscape, oil painting style. Hand-authored 2D digital painting; no image generation, stock assets or 3D.
